summary.en: Inventory is capital standing still. Why firms hold it, what it really costs, and how it absorbs uncertainty.
summary.zh: 库存就是静止不动的资金。企业为什么持有它、它的真实成本有多高，以及它如何吸收不确定性。

definition.en: Inventory is any raw material, work-in-process or finished good held in anticipation of future demand.
definition.zh: 库存是为了满足未来需求而持有的原材料、在制品或成品。

whyItMatters.en: Inventory ties up cash and hides problems such as unreliable suppliers or inaccurate forecasts — but holding none at all leaves you unable to absorb any disruption.
whyItMatters.zh: 库存占用现金，也会掩盖供应商不稳定、预测不准等问题；但一点都不持有，则完全失去吸收扰动的能力。

summary.en: Buffer inventory carried to protect against variability in demand and supply.
summary.zh: 为应对需求和供应的波动而额外持有的缓冲库存。

definition.en: The extra inventory held above expected demand to reduce the chance of a stockout during the replenishment lead time.
definition.zh: 在补货提前期内，为降低缺货概率而在预期需求之外额外持有的库存。

whyItMatters.en: Safety stock is the price paid for uncertainty: more buffer means better service but more tied-up cash. The real question is not whether to hold it, but how much is worth holding.
whyItMatters.zh: 安全库存是为不确定性付出的代价：缓冲越多，服务水平越高，但占用的现金也越多。真正的问题不是「要不要备」，而是「备多少才划算」。

summary.en: The inventory level that triggers a new purchase or production order.
summary.zh: 触发新一轮采购或生产订单的库存水位。

definition.en: The stock position at which a replenishment order should be placed so that new stock arrives before the existing stock runs out.
definition.zh: 应当下达补货订单的库存水位，确保新货在现有库存耗尽之前到达。

whyItMatters.en: Set it too low and you stock out; set it too high and you over-order. It only works when both lead time and demand are estimated honestly.
whyItMatters.zh: 定得太低会缺货，定得太高会过量采购。它只有在提前期和需求都被诚实估计的前提下才有效。

summary.en: How many times a company cycles through its inventory in a year.
summary.zh: 一年内库存被周转更新的次数。

definition.en: A ratio comparing the cost of goods sold against the average inventory held during the same period.
definition.zh: 同一时期内销货成本与平均库存持有量之间的比值。

whyItMatters.en: Higher turnover generally means less cash trapped on shelves, but what counts as good depends entirely on the industry — comparing a supermarket with a shipbuilder says nothing.
whyItMatters.zh: 周转率越高，通常意味着积压在货架上的现金越少。但多少算好完全取决于行业——把超市和造船厂放在一起比较说明不了任何问题。

summary.en: The total time between placing an order and having the goods available.
summary.zh: 从下单到货物可用的总时间。

definition.en: The elapsed time from order placement to receipt, including order processing, production or handling, and transportation.
definition.zh: 从下单到收货所经过的时间，包括订单处理、生产或搬运，以及运输。

whyItMatters.en: Lead time is the single input that most safety-stock and reorder-point calculations depend on — and it is also the one most often underestimated.
whyItMatters.zh: 提前期是安全库存和再订货点计算中最关键的输入，同时也是最容易被低估的一项。

summary.en: Small changes in customer demand become larger and larger swings further upstream.
summary.zh: 客户需求的微小变化，会沿着供应链向上逐级放大。

definition.en: The tendency for order variability to increase at every stage moving from the retailer back to the raw material supplier.
definition.zh: 从零售商回溯到原材料供应商，订单波动幅度逐级放大的现象。

whyItMatters.en: It produces overproduction, expedited freight and chronic excess inventory. In practice it usually comes from information delay and order batching, not from customers actually changing behaviour that much.
whyItMatters.zh: 它会造成过量生产、加急运输和长期库存积压。实践中其成因通常是信息延迟与批量下单，而不是客户的真实需求真的波动得那么厉害。

summary.en: The measured ability to meet demand from available stock.
summary.zh: 用现有库存满足需求的实测能力。

definition.en: The proportion of demand met on time and in full, most commonly measured as fill rate or perfect order rate.
definition.zh: 按时、按量满足的需求占比，通常用订单满足率或完美订单率来衡量。

whyItMatters.en: Service level is traded directly against inventory cost: promising 99% instead of 95% can require far more buffer stock than the extra sales actually justify.
whyItMatters.zh: 服务水平直接与库存成本相交换：把承诺从 95% 提高到 99%，可能需要的缓冲库存远超增量销售带来的收益。

metrics.formula: Fill rate = Filled order lines ÷ Total order lines × 100%

summary.en: What a product really costs once freight, duty and handling are included.
summary.zh: 把运费、关税和杂费都算进去之后，一件商品的真实成本。

definition.en: The full cost of getting a product to its destination, including product price, freight, insurance, duties and handling fees.
definition.zh: 把产品送到目的地所发生的全部成本，包含货价、运费、保险费、关税与操作费。

whyItMatters.en: A supplier with a lower unit price can end up more expensive once freight and duty are added. Sourcing decisions made on unit price alone routinely hide the real cost.
whyItMatters.zh: 单价更低的供应商，加上运费和关税后可能反而更贵。只按单价做寻源决策，通常会掩盖真实成本。

summary.en: JIT removes waste by receiving goods only as they are needed — and leaves you exposed when the network breaks.
summary.zh: 准时制只在需要时才收货，以此消除浪费 —— 但网络一旦中断，你也会立刻暴露在风险中。

definition.en: A production and inventory approach in which materials arrive exactly when the process needs them, rather than being held in advance.
definition.zh: 一种生产与库存方式：物料在生产过程中恰好需要时才到达，而不是提前持有。

whyItMatters.en: JIT reduces inventory and exposes inefficiency, which is why it improves quality and cash flow — but it removes the buffer, so any disruption stops production almost immediately.
whyItMatters.zh: 准时制降低库存、暴露低效，因此能改善质量与现金流；但它同时拿走了缓冲，任何中断几乎都会立刻让生产停下来。

title.zh: 按单生产与备货生产（MTO / MTS）

summary.en: Two opposite answers to the same question: do you build it before or after the customer asks?
summary.zh: 同一个问题的两种相反答案：在客户下单之前生产，还是之后生产。

definition.en: Make-to-stock produces against a forecast and sells from inventory; make-to-order starts production only after a confirmed customer order.
definition.zh: 备货生产按预测生产并从库存销售；按单生产则在收到客户确认订单后才开始生产。

whyItMatters.en: This choice fixes the decoupling point of the whole chain and decides who carries the risk: forecast error in make-to-stock, delivery delay in make-to-order.
whyItMatters.zh: 这个选择决定了整条链的解耦点，也决定了风险由谁承担：备货生产承担预测误差，按单生产承担交付延迟。

summary.en: From factory to port, vessel to shelf: the stages, documents and players behind a single container.
summary.zh: 从工厂到港口、从船舶到货架：一个集装箱背后涉及的环节、单证与参与方。

definition.en: The movement of a containerised shipment from shipper to consignee, covering booking, export handling, ocean carriage, customs clearance and inland delivery.
definition.zh: 集装箱货物从发货人到收货人的全流程，涵盖订舱、出口操作、海运、清关与内陆配送。

whyItMatters.en: Most delays do not happen on the water — they happen at the handoffs: documentation errors, customs holds and missing inland capacity.
whyItMatters.zh: 大多数延误并不发生在海上，而发生在交接环节：单证错误、海关查验，以及内陆运力不足。

summary.en: Moving goods from inbound to outbound without putting them into storage.
summary.zh: 货物不进入存储环节，直接从入库侧转到出库侧。

definition.en: A distribution practice where incoming goods are sorted and loaded directly onto outbound vehicles, with little or no storage in between.
definition.zh: 一种配送做法：到货经分拣后直接装上出港车辆，中间几乎不经过存储。

whyItMatters.en: It cuts storage cost and handling time, but only works with reliable inbound timing and accurate advance information — otherwise the dock itself becomes the bottleneck.
whyItMatters.zh: 它能降低仓储成本、缩短搬运时间，但前提是到货时间可靠、预先信息准确，否则月台本身会变成瓶颈。

summary.en: How to identify, assess and mitigate disruption before it reaches the customer.
summary.zh: 如何在中断影响到客户之前，识别、评估并降低风险。

definition.en: The systematic identification, assessment and mitigation of disruptions before they reach the customer.
definition.zh: 在中断影响到客户之前，系统地识别、评估并降低风险。

whyItMatters.en: Risk cannot be eliminated, only repositioned: dual sourcing, buffer inventory and better visibility each cost something. The real decision is which exposure is acceptable.
whyItMatters.zh: 风险无法消除，只能重新摆放：双源采购、缓冲库存和信息可见性各有代价。真正的决策是哪种敞口可以接受。
